translations.translatedText: # Wednesday 1.1.2020 (radio)
The President gave a New Year's speech. The police had a busy New Year's. Many fires broke out on New Year's Eve. The Clear News TV broadcast starts from a new broadcast location.
Listen
You can read the news at the same time below.
## The President gave a New Year's speech

![The President of the Republic, Sauli Niinistö, before recording the President's traditional New Year's speech at the Presidential Palace in Helsinki on New Year's Eve, 31 December 2019.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_4928,h_2772,x_0,y_254/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-6272245e0c9e44e2d29/1577885333)
Open image viewer
The President of the Republic, Sauli Niinistö, recorded his New Year's speech at the Presidential Palace. Photo: Mikko Stig / Lehtikuva
President Sauli Niinistö has given the traditional New Year's speech of the President on television.
The President spoke about many things. For example, he expressed concern about the Prime Minister's work pressures, and said that the government must support the Prime Minister in joint decisions.

The President also drew attention once again to how the way Finns discuss things has changed. The President said that in discussions people no longer seek a shared view, but deliberately misunderstand each other. This creates room for half-truths and lies.

The President also said that hate speech and targeting people have become more common. He said that freedom of speech does not, however, give the right to violate another person's honour or to incite hatred against a group of people.
The President also demanded that nurses, teachers and police have the right to do their work in peace, without harassment and threats.
## The police had a busy New Year

![Children and adults watching children's fireworks at the children's New Year party organised by the city of Helsinki at Kansalaistori on 31 December 2019.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11140683)
Open image viewer
Fireworks at Helsinki's Kansalaistori. Photo: Vesa Moilanen / Lehtikuva
New Year's celebrations have brought a lot of work for the police in different parts of the country.
The police received many reports of, for example, noise, assaults and fights in homes and in public places.

The police also received many reports of fireworks rockets that were misused. The police say that rockets were fired at people, houses and cars. For example, in Helsinki, Turku, Oulu and Kuopio, groups of youths fired rockets into crowds.
Fireworks rockets have also caused eye injuries. At least 4 people have been treated in hospitals for eye injuries.
## Fires kept firefighters busy

![A terraced house burned in Klaukkala in Nurmijärvi on New Year's night, 1 January 2020.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_1980,h_1114,x_0,y_65/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-6272075e0c02963ac75/1577845464)
Open image viewer
A terraced house burned in Nurmijärvi on New Year's night. Photo: Vesa Moilanen/ Lehtikuva
Rescue services have also had a lot of work. A lot of fires broke out during last evening and last night.

For example, in Nurmijärvi a terraced house with 5 flats burned. In Koskela in Helsinki a fire broke out on the balcony of a 5-storey building. The fire also spread inside a flat and into the roof structure of the building. In Pori a firework flew onto a detached house's balcony and started a fire. In Joensuu the fire destroyed the Huvitörmä dance hall.
However, no one was injured in the fires.
## Croatia becomes EU president

![Prime Minister Marin handed over the "chairmanship ball" to Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković at the European Council on 13 December.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11137173)
Open image viewer
Croatian Prime Minister Andrej Plenković and Finnish Prime Minister Sanna Marin. Photo: Anne Sjöholm / Prime Minister's Office
Croatia begins today as the EU's new presidency, after Finland.
Croatia is the youngest member state of the EU. It joined the union in the summer of 2013.
Croatia is now EU president for the first time. The presidency lasts half a year.
## New airtime for the Clear News TV
The easy-language TV news will be shown on television again tomorrow, Thursday. However, the airtime is new.
This year, the easy-language TV news will be shown on weekdays on TV1 at 16:40.
